description: Clear (mark read & dismiss) or delete a previously-sent ntfy notification by `sequence_id`. Append-only: the original message stays in cache and a `message_clear`/`message_delete` event is emitted to subscribers. Re-issuing the same operation is safe — message state does not change, but a fresh event fires each time. ntfy.sh accepts unknown sequence IDs without error; stricter ntfy variants surface a `not_found` failure. The first call always asks the user to confirm the topic, `sequence_id`, and operation and comes back requesting that input rather than a result; reissue the same call with the answer attached to carry it out. Declining fails the call with `consent_declined`.

base_url.description: Override the configured `NTFY_BASE_URL` for this call — an absolute `http(s)://` URL. When the override differs from the configured base URL, server-configured auth credentials are NOT forwarded.

operation.description: What to do: `clear` marks the notification read & dismisses it (subscribers see `message_clear`); `delete` removes it from the drawer (subscribers see `message_delete`). Safe to re-issue — the original message stays in cache, but a fresh event is emitted to subscribers each call.

sequence_id.description: Identifier of the previously-published message. Same value used as `sequence_id` on `ntfy_publish_message`. 1–64 chars, `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]`.

topic.description: Topic the message was published to. Required unless NTFY_DEFAULT_TOPIC is set.

name: ntfy_manage_message

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `consent_declined`: The user was asked to confirm the clear/delete and declined, cancelled, or answered with a payload that did not parse. `forbidden_topic`: Auth required for the target topic. `not_found`: Stricter ntfy variants returned 404 because the sequence_id was never published to this topic, or the cache window has elapsed; ntfy.sh accepts unknown sequences without error. `upstream_unreachable`: DNS, connection, or network failure reaching the ntfy server after retries were exhausted. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

event_id.description: Server-assigned ID of the emitted `message_clear` / `message_delete` event — distinct from the original message `sequence_id` it references.

sequence_id.description: Sequence ID of the original message the event references.

time.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when ntfy emitted the event.

topic.description: Topic the event was emitted on.

title: Ntfy Manage Message
